docs.title: Welcome to My Data Science & AI Portfolio
Building Solutions Through Data & Intelligence
docs.text: Welcome! This space showcases my personal journey of expanding my expertise in Python, Machine Learning, and applied Artificial Intelligence. I believe that data is more than just numbers—it is a powerful tool for discovering hidden patterns and solving complex, contemporary problems. Through hands-on projects, rigorous data exploration, and continuous learning, I transform raw information into meaningful, domain-driven narratives and predictive solutions. Explore my featured projects below to see how I bridge the gap between clean code, analytical thinking, and real-world AI applications. Let’s connect and build the future together!

docs.title: About Me
docs.text:
I am a passionate explorer of data with a relentless drive to master modern technologies. My journey began with a deep dive into Python and data manipulation, which naturally evolved into a fascination with Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence. What sets my approach apart is my focus on domain-driven exploration. I don't just apply algorithms blindly; I look at datasets from a unique, personal perspective to truly understand the core logic of the problem at hand—whether it is analyzing historical socioeconomic patterns or uncovering subtle morphological traits in nature.

On a personal level, I am a peaceful, non-confrontational individual who is naturally inclined to reflect deeply on various aspects of the surrounding world. This reflective mindset heavily influences how I work with data: I always try to do my absolute best to solve the problems posed to me, even if it requires digging deeper and going the extra mile to find the right solution. At the same time, I value collaboration and am never afraid to ask for help when necessary. I also strongly believe in community, always striving to help others and enthusiastically sharing my knowledge with those around me.

docs.title: 📝 Project Overview
docs.text:
Friend Finder & Peer Matching Dashboard is an innovative, data-driven application that utilizes unsupervised machine learning to connect people with similar traits, hobbies, and interests. Based on an expanded survey dataset (v2), the app automatically groups participants into distinct peer communities.

Instead of relying on basic keyword filtering, I implemented an AI-Native clustering pipeline. Users input their demographic details, preferred locations, and favorite animals, and the system instantly matches them with their closest community. By feeding the statistical centroids of each cluster into OpenAI's Large Language Models (LLMs), the application dynamically synthesizes warm, relatable group names and behavioral profiles (e.g., "Miłośnicy Lasów i Psów"), helping users discover how many like-minded friends they have within the dataset.

docs.title: 🚀 Core Features & ML Methodology
docs.text: The updated v2 pipeline integrates advanced data grouping, cluster profiling, and automated generative AI text enrichment:

docs.title: 📊 1. Multi-Dimensional Peer Clustering & EDA
docs.text:
• Exploratory Data Analysis: Conducted a rigorous initial analysis using Seaborn and Matplotlib to map out customer demographics and profile behavior patterns across different user categories.
  • Optimal Group Identification: Developed an unsupervised learning pipeline to automatically cluster survey respondents into 8 distinct interest-based peer communities.
  • Centroid Profiling: Extracted the precise statistical averages for each group, defining the common traits, shared locations, and unique habits that connect people within each cluster.

docs.title: 🤖 2. Generative AI Community Profiling
docs.text:
• OpenAI LLM Integration: Automated the interpretation of abstract mathematical groups by passing the statistical distribution of each cluster to OpenAI's models via engineered prompts.
  • Dynamic Group Descriptions: The system automatically crafts engaging group names and friendly summaries, explaining the shared profile of the community you belong to.

docs.title: 🛠️ 3. Cloud Deployment & Iterative Upgrades
docs.text:
• Streamlit Cloud Infrastructure: Successfully migrated and deployed the modern dashboard architecture onto the Streamlit Community Cloud for public access.
  • Iterative Core Updates: Upgraded the underlying models and raw data assets from the original codebase to the newer v2 standard.

docs.title: 🛠️ Infrastructure & Tech Stack
docs.text:
• Frontend & UI: Streamlit (Python-native interactive community dashboard).
  • Automated Machine Learning: PyCaret (used for rapid prototyping, model conversion, and real-time user-to-cluster assignment via predict_model).
  • Data Visualization: Plotly Express (for production-ready dynamic charts) and Seaborn / Matplotlib (for analytical EDA phase).
  • Generative AI Enrichment: OpenAI API (GPT models for automated community name and profile synthesis).
  • Cloud Deployment: Streamlit Community Cloud (Python 3.11 environment optimized with fixed environment dependencies).

docs.title: 📝 Project Overview
docs.text:
Half-Marathon Finish Time Predictor is an end-to-end Machine Learning web application designed to predict a runner's final finish time based on their demographic profile and early-race performance.

Instead of building a generic black-box tool, I approached this project from a domain-focused perspective to solve a real athletic dilemma: How can a runner accurately estimate their final pace and manage their energy based on their initial performance? The app transforms real race metrics into actionable, real-time predictions, providing a highly practical tool for endurance athletes.

docs.title: 🚀 Core Features & ML Methodology
docs.text: The project encompasses a full machine learning lifecycle, from raw data processing to cloud deployment:

docs.title: 📚 1. Advanced EDA & Outlier Filtering
docs.text:
• Physical Threshold Filtering: Implemented constraints (e.g., minimum 5km split and total times) to automatically protect the pipeline against obvious timing system glitches.
  • Tukey’s IQR Method: Applied the Interquartile Range method to isolate and remove extreme mathematical outliers (elite athletes and walkers). This successfully regularized the regression process on the behavior of 98% of recreational runners.

docs.title: 🤖 2. Model Routing & Prototyping (PyCaret)
docs.text:
• Automated Prototyping: Utilized the PyCaret library to rapidly benchmark and evaluate over a dozen different regression architectures with various parameters on the feature matrix.
  • Ridge Regression Optimization: Through systematic comparison, I determined that Ridge Regression offered the highest accuracy and the most robust regularization against overfitting for this specific dataset.

docs.title: 🛠️ 3. Resource-Optimized Production Pipeline
docs.text:
• Pure Scikit-Learn Conversion: To optimize server resource usage and ensure a lightweight deployment, I decoupled the final model from heavy automated frameworks and rebuilt the entire training and tuning process inside a native Scikit-Learn pipeline.
  • Hyperparameter Tuning & Cloud Storage: Implemented fine-grained hyperparameter tuning via GridSearchCV, achieving results equal to or better than the automated baseline. The serialized model (.pkl) is fetched on demand by the application hosted on Render, creating a cost-effective, zero-ops infrastructure.

docs.title: 🛠️ Infrastructure & Tech Stack
docs.text:
• Frontend & UI: Streamlit (Python-native interactive dashboard).
  • Automated Machine Learning: PyCaret (used for rapid prototyping and model comparison).
  • Production Machine Learning: Scikit-Learn (used for the final production pipeline), Pandas, NumPy.
  • Cloud Deployment: Render.com (Web Service hosting under a free-tier resource constraint).
  • Model Management: Serialized joblib pipeline architecture with external cloud model fetching.

docs.title: My Perspective on the Iris Dataset: A Domain-Focused Exploratory Analysis
docs.text:
In this portfolio project, I conducted an Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) on the classic Iris dataset, a staple in data science and machine learning. The dataset contains 150 samples across three distinct species—Iris setosa, Iris versicolor, and Iris virginica—with exactly 50 observations for each. My analysis focused on four critical morphological measurements recorded in centimeters: sepal length, sepal width, petal length, and petal width, with each row representing an individual flower.

Instead of just running standard algorithms, I approached this data from a personal perspective to uncover how individual physical dimensions differ across species. My analysis revealed distinct morphological boundaries between the groups, showing that depending on the specific floral traits you prioritize, each species exhibits unique structural advantages. Ultimately, Iris virginica consistently proved to have the largest overall dimensions, Iris setosa stood out with wide sepals but minimal petal sizes, while Iris versicolor serves as a beautifully balanced middle ground.

docs.title: 📝 Project Overview
docs.text:
Lingilo is an advanced, AI-powered web application designed to comprehensively support foreign language learning. It combines traditional memorization techniques (Spaced Repetition) with the power of Large Language Models (LLMs), semantic search, and speech transcription.

Lingilo is not just another translator – it is an intelligent environment that helps users understand context, analyze grammar, practice pronunciation, and systematically acquire new vocabulary.

docs.title: 📸 System Screenshots
docs.text: Login & Welcome Screen Main Application Dashboard Smart Flashcards (SM-2) Text Correction Module

docs.title: 🚀 Core Features & Learning Modules
docs.text: The application offers 6 main modes to support users at every stage of their learning journey:

docs.title: 📚 1. Smart Flashcards & Spaced Repetition System (SM-2)
docs.text:
• SM-2 Algorithm: Features a built-in Spaced Repetition algorithm that optimizes learning time by showing words exactly when users are about to forget them.
  • AI Flashcard Creator: Just by typing a single word, the AI automatically generates its base form, grammatical features (case, tense, gender), definitions, inflections, and example sentences with translations.
  • Authentic Context: Integration with the open Tatoeba database allows fetching real-life example sentences with a single click.

docs.title: ✍️ 2. Text Correction with Explanations
docs.text: • Analyzes text written in a foreign language. The AI not only corrects grammatical and stylistic errors but also explains point-by-point why the changes were made and what caused the mistakes.

docs.title: 🗣️ 3. Pronunciation Training & Audio Generation (TTS)
docs.text:
• Converts any text or translated sentence into natural-sounding speech (Text-To-Speech) to practice the correct accent.
  • Allows recording personal pronunciations and attaching them directly to the flashcards.

docs.title: 🎙️ 4. Voice Notes with Transcription
docs.text: • Records voice notes in a foreign language, and the system automatically transcribes them into text using advanced speech recognition models, perfect for practicing spontaneous speaking.

docs.title: 🧠 5. Knowledge Base with Semantic Search
docs.text:
• All translations, expert queries, and voice notes are saved in the asynchronous database.
  • Searches are performed "by meaning" (vector-based). If a user searches for "pets", the system finds notes containing "dog" or "cat", even if the exact keyword isn't present in the text.

docs.title: 💬 6. Chat with a Language Expert
docs.text: • A dedicated module to ask complex linguistic questions (e.g., "What is the difference between 'make' and 'do' in English?") and receive a comprehensive, educational explanation from the AI.

docs.title: 🤖 AI Models Used & Their Roles
docs.text: Lingilo is a truly AI-Native system utilizing specialized models for complex pipeline tasks:

docs.title: 1. Large Language Models (LLMs) — Groq & OpenAI
docs.text: Provides precise translations, error corrections, and expert chats. It allows users to choose between lightning-fast, free open-source models via the Groq cloud (e.g., the Llama 3 family) and advanced models from OpenAI (e.g., gpt-4o), featuring a safe fallback to Groq if a paid API key is missing.

docs.title: 2. Instructor + Pydantic (Structured Outputs)
docs.text: Forces unstructured LLM text outputs into strict, validated JSON objects based on Pydantic models. Used for parsing grammatical features (extracting tense, number, person, case) securely before adding entries to the database.

docs.title: 3. Whisper Model (whisper-large-v3)
docs.text: An advanced multilingual speech recognition model run asynchronously via OpenAI / Groq API to transcribe user voice recordings into clean text.

docs.title: 4. Vector Models (sentence-transformers)
docs.text: Uses a locally loaded paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 model to generate multi-dimensional vector embeddings, powering the deep semantic search engine.

docs.title: 5. AI Telemetry — Langfuse
docs.text: Integrated using the direct HTTP API (generation-create) to track every AI trace, count token consumption (promptTokens, completionTokens), monitor production API costs, and evaluate generation quality latency.

docs.title: 🛠️ Infrastructure & Tech Stack
docs.text:
• Frontend & UI: Streamlit, Streamlit OAuth (Auth0 secure login).
  • Backend & Async Core: Python 3.11 using native asyncio for high-performance event loop pooling.
  • Database Layer: Asynchronous SQLAlchemy + PostgreSQL (compatible with Neon DB) or SQLite for local environments.
  • AI Routing & Tools: LiteLLM (universal API router), Instructor, Sentence-Transformers.

docs.title: 💥 Production Case Study: Resolving AWS WebSocket Cookie Drops
docs.text: !!! danger "Production Issue (Streamlit Community Cloud Infrastructure)" During deployment on Streamlit Community Cloud (AWS server nodes), users faced random logouts upon pressing F5 (Hard Refresh). Investigation revealed that the cloud reverse proxy servers stripped cookie headers during WebSocket upgrade handshakes (GET /_stcore/stream), leading to an empty cookie dict inside Python. Furthermore, executing standard async JavaScript components to poll cookies froze the frontend React render cycle, causing the Auth0 login button to completely disappear from the landing page. This issue was absent in the local development environment (localhost).

docs.title: 🛠️ Applied Engineering Solution
docs.text:
The bug was mitigated by decoupling the unstable JS cookie management from the unauthenticated landing layout view and implementing a highly stable Hybrid Query Params Fallback strategy:

# Synchronous native URL query param parsing for F5 persistence
url_token = st.query_params.get("session_token")
if url_token and str(url_token).strip() != "" and url_token != "None":
    st.session_state.token = {"access_token": url_token}
    st.rerun()
  1. Address Bar Token Mapping: Upon successful Auth0 redirection, the access token payload is captured and appended safely as a secure query parameter (?session_token=...) directly to the address bar. Since AWS reverse proxies do not strip URL parameters during WebSocket switches, the application securely extracts the token on fresh page loads.
  2. Unconditional UI Rendering: The login interface layout was fully insulated from any async initialization blockers. The Auth0 action button renders instantly as pure HTML/JS, ensuring absolute interface stability and preventing rendering deadlocks.

docs.title: 🔄 Native Trade Executor & Cross-Terminal Trade Copier for MT4/MT5
docs.text:
Project Status: Closed Beta 3 (Distributed Testing) Supported Platforms: MetaTrader 4 (MQL4) & MetaTrader 5 (MQL5)

docs.title: 📝 Project Overview
docs.text:
Trade Executor is an advanced, native Expert Advisor written in MQL4 and MQL5 that transforms standard MetaTrader 4 and MetaTrader 5 terminals into programmable web servers. Operating as a localized receiver module, the script listens for incoming secure webhooks and JSON payloads, allowing for instantaneous execution of trades sent directly from TradingView, custom Python scripts, analytical backends, or a companion native Sender module (MT4/MT5) that I also developed, effectively enabling high-speed, local cross-terminal trade copying,.

The primary engineering challenge in this project was bypassing the inherent limitations of the MetaTrader environment regarding asynchronous and multi-threaded network communication. Instead of relying on external, paid cloud bridge services that compromise data privacy, I developed a decentralized, local architecture that manages symbol mapping, lot sizing, and Stop Loss/Take Profit levels directly at the MQL terminal level,.

docs.title: 🚀 Core Features & Infrastructure Engineering
docs.text: The production-ready Trade Executor module implements low-level system communication while enforcing rigorous risk management procedures:

docs.title: 🌐 1. Low-Level TCP/HTTP Server & Trade Copier Integration
docs.text:
• Local Cross-Terminal Trade Copying: Pairs seamlessly with a native Sender module attached to a master terminal, creating a highly stable, real-time trade replication system across multiple MetaTrader instances on the same machine or a remote VPS.
  • Native WinSockets Support: I bypassed MetaTrader's native network limitations by directly binding the MQL scripts to low-level Windows network libraries (winsock) via DLL imports, achieving sub-millisecond execution speeds.
  • Multi-Port Listening: The server architecture allows the script to listen on multiple customizable ports simultaneously (e.g., 9090, 9091), enabling a single instance on a chart to aggregate and segregate trade traffic from multiple strategies or signal providers.

docs.title: 🤖 2. Advanced Position & Risk Management
docs.text:
• Simulated Netting Module: I programmed a simulated netting engine that functions on both MT4 and MT5 hedging accounts. It automatically calculates total net exposure and, if necessary, reduces or reverses positions using native sub-routines (partial closes), ensuring compliance with strict prop-firm drawdown rules.
  • Volatility Protection (Slippage Guard): Implemented a price slippage filter (Slippage) that safely rejects orders if market volatility moves the price beyond defined broker points before the broker processes the ticket. In case of rejection, the script triggers an automated OrderRetries sequence with a controlled delay to protect the broker's server from spamming.
  • Replay Attack Protection: The script automatically rejects orders whose timestamps fall outside the defined MaxSignalAgeSec security window, protecting the account from executing old signals.

docs.title: 🛠️ 3. Cross-Broker Synchronization & Translation
docs.text:
• Dynamic Symbol Mapping: Designed a flexible instrument name translation engine (e.g., automatically converting an incoming NASUSD ticker from TradingView to the local broker's equivalent NAS100.cash or appending specific prefixes and suffixes).
  • Audit Trail Preservation: The script for the MT4 platform automatically appends the original source order ID to partial close comments, guaranteeing full historical transparency and continuity of the account history.

docs.title: 🛠️ Infrastructure & Tech Stack
docs.text:
• Runtime Environment: Native Expert Advisor scripts written in MQL4 (MetaTrader 4) and MQL5 (MetaTrader 5).
  • System Communication: Direct interaction with low-level Windows networking libraries (C++ DLL integration & WinSockets).
  • Data Protocol: Strictly formatted JSON POST requests using dot-decimal notation for all numeric values.
  • Network Architecture: Localized HTTP/TCP REST Server (Loopback interface binding on 127.0.0.1 for local copying or 0.0.0.0 binding to listen for external signals).

docs.title: 📡 Native Trade Broadcaster & Cross-Terminal Master Synchronization Engine for MT4/MT5
docs.text:
Project Status: Closed Beta 3 (Distributed Testing) Supported Platforms: MetaTrader 4 (MQL4) & MetaTrader 5 (MQL5)

Sender's Panel Sender's Settings

docs.title: 📝 Project Overview
docs.text:
Trade Broadcaster is a high-performance, native Expert Advisor written in MQL4 and MQL5 designed to monitor MetaTrader accounts in real-time and instantly stream market and pending order payloads to any designated receiver endpoint. It serves as the powerful "Master" component in a decoupled architecture, allowing traders to broadcast trades to local or remote trade execution engines (Trade Executors), custom Python APIs, or third-party cloud webhooks.

The primary engineering focus of this broadcaster was ensuring absolute synchronization and data integrity under resource-constrained environments or network failures. By bypassing MetaTrader's native web limits, the script achieves sub-millisecond execution captured at the terminal's core and features sophisticated automated state recovery systems. This guarantees that no execution payload (open, close, modify, or cancel) is ever dropped or duplicated, maintaining a perfect mirror account across target destinations.

docs.title: 🚀 Core Features & Infrastructure Engineering
docs.text: The native MQL-based Broadcaster module implements low-level event capturing, granular trade filtering, and smart synchronization recovery systems:

docs.title: 🌐 1. Ultra-Low Latency Signal Streaming & Multi-Target Copying
docs.text:
• Native WinSockets Serialization: Bypassed the terminal's built-in WebRequest latency by using direct DLL imports of Windows Socket libraries (winsock), allowing the script to resolve and stream JSON POST payloads directly via the operating system.
  • Simultaneous Multi-Target Broadcasting: Engineered with a highly scalable data routing system (InpExtraTargets), enabling the master terminal to copy and broadcast transactions to multiple independent remote PCs or servers at the exact same millisecond (Format: URL|Route, URL|Route).

docs.title: 🤖 2. Smart Sync Recovery & State Persistence (New in Beta 3)
docs.text:
• Smart Offline Actions Sync: Programmed a persistent state machine (InpSyncOfflineActions) that logs account states directly to physical disk. Upon terminal crash or system restart, the Sender reads its last saved state, cross-checks it with the broker's server, and automatically broadcasts any missing safe actions (close/cancel/update) to correct the slave terminals.
  • On-Resume Hot Syncing: Integrated a real-time thread synchronization mechanism (InpSyncOnResume) that triggers a microsecond audit and catch-up broadcast whenever the EA is unpaused or Algo Trading is toggled back on.
  • Exponential Backoff Network Safety: Implemented a network throttling safeguard (InpMaxRetries). In the event of an internet or receiver timeout, the Sender intelligently backs off using an exponential waiting curve (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, etc.), preventing network congestion while ensuring trade safety.

docs.title: 🛠️ 3. Granular Filtering & Outgoing Translation
docs.text:
• Magic Number & Manual Filters: Designed built-in filtering layers allowing the user to whitelist specific Expert Advisor Magic Numbers or strictly isolate manually executed human trades (InpCopyManualOnly), completely ignoring background automated noise.
  • Pre-Transmission Lot Scaling: Features a pre-sending multiplier (QtyMultiplier) that scales lot sizes directly on the master side before the data payload is generated and broadcasted.
  • Outgoing Symbol Mapping: Translates local broker-specific instrument symbols (e.g., custom suffixes like EURUSD.pro or unique index tags like WS30) into clean, standardized tickers (EURUSD or US30) before data serialization.

docs.title: 🛠️ Infrastructure & Tech Stack
docs.text:
• Runtime Environment: Native Expert Advisor scripts written in MQL4 (MetaTrader 4) and MQL5 (MetaTrader 5).
  • System Communication: Low-level integration with Windows Socket libraries via C++ DLL execution.
  • Data Protocol: Structured JSON POST payloads utilizing dot-decimal formatting.
  • Network Routing Architecture: Advanced endpoint string append formatting (InpRoute), allowing multiple distinct strategy payloads to be multiplexed to the exact same receiving port.

docs.title: Echoes of the Titanic: My Analytical Journey Through Passenger Survival Data
docs.text:
In this project, I performed an in-depth Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) on the historic Titanic passenger dataset using the Pandas library. Rather than treat it as a routine training exercise, I approached the data as a real-world investigative project, exploring the demographics and survival outcomes of the passengers on board. My analysis involved profiling key attributes such as travel class (pclass), age, sex, family connections (sibsp, parch), and ticket fare, all with the goal of uncovering the hidden human patterns and structural dynamics behind one of history's most tragic maritime disasters.

By driving the exploration through my unique analytical lens, I was able to quantify the exact socio-economic and demographic disparities in survival rates. It is important to note that these calculated percentages reflect the specific dataset provided, which does not encompass every single passenger on the actual voyage. Nevertheless, the data clearly confirmed a stark priority toward rescuing women and children, while revealing how heavily this privilege was tied to wealth: over 96% of first-class women survived, compared to under 50% in third class. Ultimately, my analysis showed that first-class passengers had the highest overall survival rate in this sample at nearly 62%, whereas third-class passengers faced the lowest odds at just 25%.
